result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: addGuests.handler.ts computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) for the DB write, but calls `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input. email-manager.ts then chooses `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` via `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so an already-registered attendee whose email was re-submitted is misclassified and receives a full 'scheduled' email instead of the 'new guests added' notice. The wrong-template selection for duplicates/blacklisted addresses is a real correctness defect

judged_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests rather than uniqueGuests, so the newGuests.includes(attendee.email) check in email-manager.ts classifies already-existing attendees whose address was re-submitted as newly added. An existing attendee whose email was re-typed receives a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail ('you are scheduled') instead of the 'new guests added' notice, and blacklisted addresses that were filtered out of the database write still steer which template each attendee gets.
